newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Beijing Yanshan seeks Hong Kong listing.
newsitem.headline: China's Beijing Yanshan seeks Hong Kong listing.

text.p: China's state-owned Beijing Yanshan Petrochemical Corp has applied for central government permission to list in Hong Kong, a company official said on Tuesday.
Yanshan expected to issue shares representing about half of its 12 billion yuan assets, the official said by telephone.
It was not clear when Yanshan would be granted permission to list, and even after permission was given the company would still need time to prepare its accounts, he said.
China strictly controls the number of firms allowed to issue Chinese H shares on the Hong Kong market.

The Financial News newspaper said last November that Yanshan, one of China's biggest petrochemical companies, held 6.5 billion yuan in fixed assets and 5.5 billion yuan in working assets, with total liabilities of around 6.0 billion yuan.
The firm had sharply increased sales because of efficient capital turnover, sound asset structure and a low level of debt compared with other Chinese state-owned firms, the newspaper said.
